subtopic: Share Class Eligibility and Account Types
source_evidence: many mutual funds make these shares available to retail investors without requiring a high initial investment minimum through various means, including through an employer (e.g., through a retirement plan) or through an investment advisory account.
question: Misconception: Class I shares are available only to institutional investors, not to retail investors or through retirement and advisory accounts.
answer: Class I shares may be available to retail investors through certain arrangements, including an employer-sponsored retirement plan or an investment advisory account. Availability and investment minimums can vary by fund, so Class I shares are not automatically limited to institutional investors.
